purpose: Naval gameplay on the generated world. The naval_missions probe (src/MNBL.ProceduralWorld/Automation/NavalMissionsProbe.cs) reads its world, designated test save and rules from this file; tools/summarize_naval_missions.py checks every case below against the run's outputs and writes evidence/gameplay/naval-scenarios.json. A failure found by a run or the review is added to regressions with what now guards it.

stockMissingPatterns: ^Voice object for text id is not found:

cases.what: A ship bought at a port town as the port screen's Done buys it (War Sails' PortScreenTradeModeHandler for the town and the player: its buy button enabled, OnBuyShip, then OnConfirmChanges, which pays ShipCostModel's trade value and docks the new fleet at the town), then a ship damaged (Ship.OnShipDamaged, recorded setup) and repaired through the port menu's repair (RepairShipAction for each damaged docked ship, at the model's repair cost).

Embarkation and a port-to-port voyage: the town's port, the port menu's set sail (at sea at the port), the voyage to another port town of the main land group as a map click orders it (NavigationHelper.GetInteractionDataForMainParty: naval navigation, the port targeted), campaign time running until the party arrives (sampled hourly, every sample on naval navigation), the destination's port menu (on land in the town, the fleet docked), its town center and the leave path (on land at the gate). The voyage starts where the previous step's leave path put the party.
The same voyage from the mainland to an island's port town (a land group other than the main one, in the same basin).

A village drop-off: from the island's port town aboard to a harbour village's port (the village menu with the party still at sea), the menu's disembark (on land at the village's gate, the fleet at its port), then back aboard at the anchor as a click on it orders it (MobileParty.SetMoveGoToInteractablePoint; the anchor's interaction sets sail at it). Then a coastal landing as a click on land orders it (MapState.ProcessTravel: the sea-to-land transition, on land navigation, the anchor left at the coast) and back aboard at that anchor.

Targeted regression seeds: world A (seed 42) with the voyages' settlements, the raid's village and the blockade's town pinned in this file, and every voyage's narrowest water (the water's width across 8 axes, away from both ends of the voyage) recorded, so a regression replays the same straits and coastal towns.

AI sea travel while the cases run: AI parties take to the sea and land (War Sails' OnMobilePartyNavigationStateChangedEvent), each checked an hour later on its domain's navigation, and parties arrive from the sea at port towns (a landing and the town's entry in the same tick), island port towns among them.

Pirates against C06 and W03: MMR-35's pirate spawn points served by MMR-39's naval scene wrapper, per pirate clan as many as the plan gives it and each on naval navigation; War Sails' patrol zones exactly the served points (as many zones as served points, each one of them; the scene's own spawn points, the installed Calradia coordinates' source, are 0 by construction on the generated scene); the pirate parties of the pirate clans at sea, on naval navigation, each assigned a served zone.

A pirate encounter ending in a retreat: the party at sea and a pirate party beside it (recorded setup, the pirate sent back to patrol its zone after), the campaign's encounter with its at-sea meeting marked done (the meeting is a conversation mission), the encounter menu's attack: a naval map event of exactly the two parties, the naval battle mission on the patch's naval scene, every spawn checked, then left (OnEndMissionResult, a retreat) and the encounter left; the party back at sea within the naval return bound, on naval navigation.

A naval defeat leading to capture: the party, cut to a crew that all goes aboard, loses a naval battle with another pirate party on the patch's naval scene (every agent of its side falls), the player taken prisoner (the defeat menu answered if it shows), the escape forced (EndCaptivityAction.ApplyByEscape), at sea War Sails' raft menus (the raft, its wait and its end menu), campaign time running until the raft washes ashore; the party on land, out of raft state, on land navigation.

A seaborne village raid, distinct from a naval field battle: a harbour village of another kingdom (war declared for it, peace made after, recorded), the voyage to it, its menu at sea, the hostile action's raid, the encounter's attack with the naval troop selection answered with the troops and ships it offers, the naval raid mission on the village's center scene in its naval_raid level with its landing setup and War Sails' landing run (the player's agents ashore), the defenders killed by the probe, the raid's wait menu until the village is looted, its end menu with the ended map events recorded; the party still at sea by the village's port, its return checked at sea within the naval bound.

A coastal blockade, distinct from a naval field battle: a port town of another kingdom besieged from land by the party owning its fleet (a siege cannot start from the sea), War Sails' SiegeEvent activating the blockade, the player's anchor disabled, the town's blockade arcs (BlockadePositionScript on MMR-40's arc entities) on naval navigation for the fleet and for the script's full arcs, then the siege lifted through the menu (the blockade deactivated, the anchor enabled) and the party moved back to where the case found it.

No missing asset and valid spawns: no engine log line during a case names a generated object or an opened scene as missing and every other missing line is a stock kind (stockMissingPatterns); no engine assert; in every mission every active human agent stands on the navigation mesh or a scene object (a ship's deck, a seat) inside the boundaries.
No game and every tracked static at its baseline at the start and at the end; the run's rules are the scenario file's.

regressions.failure: The port menu's repair threw a NullReferenceException in GameMenuManager.RefreshMenuOptions; every later step of the chain then failed (the reload lost the fleet).
regressions.cause: The repair's consequence repairs every damaged docked ship, then refreshes the menu through its view's handler (MenuContext.Handler.OnMenuRefresh); the probe ran the option in the frame the menu opened, before the view had attached its handler.
regressions.fix: Options whose consequence refreshes the menu wait for the menu context's handler (two frames more).

guard.check: the port menu's repair restored the ship

regressions.failure: Five AI villager parties were recorded at sea on no valid campaign position.
regressions.cause: A party created at sea (War Sails' fishing parties) raises OnMobilePartyNavigationStateChangedEvent from MobileParty.InitializeMobilePartyAtPosition before its position is set; the probe read the position at the event.
regressions.fix: Each transition's party is checked an hour later (HourlyTickEvent), on its domain's navigation then, unless in a settlement or a transition.

guard.check: every AI party checked an hour after its transition

regressions.failure: After the naval raid's victory the raid never progressed: the case timed out at raiding_village, and the next case reloaded the save.
regressions.cause: The victory pushes the party screen (prisoners) and the inventory (loot) before the raid's wait menu; the probe closed only the inventory.
regressions.fix: Every loot screen of a victory is closed as the player closes it (the party screen, the inventory, War Sails' port screen in loot mode), counted, and the raid's wait menu runs campaign time.

regressions.failure: After the raid the case timed out at village_raid_ended_leaded_by_someone_else.
regressions.cause: VillageHostileActionCampaignBehavior.OnMapEventEnded shows village_raid_ended_leaded_by_someone_else, not village_player_raid_ended, when the raid's map event was not led by the player's party, as after the naval raid.
regressions.fix: Both end menus are answered with their continue; the menu shown is recorded.

guard.check: still at sea after the raid

regressions.failure: The raid scene's landing points counted 0 although the naval raid ran.
regressions.cause: NavalRaidMissionController finds the landing paths by tag expression (landing(_\d+)*, then landing_00<ship> per frame), not by an exact tag.
regressions.fix: The landing and jumping entities are counted with the controller's tag expressions; the player's spawn frame by its tag.

guard.check: the naval raid opened the village's center scene

regressions.failure: The raid's return failed with 'the party returned off land' although the party was by the village's port at sea, as a seaborne raid leaves it.
regressions.cause: MMR-52's shared return check required land.
regressions.fix: The return check takes the domain: a seaborne raid's return is checked at sea within the naval bound.

guard.check: the raid's return checked at sea

regressions.failure: After every agent of the player's side fell in the naval mission, the encounter menu came back (attack, send ships, leave) and the player was not captured.
regressions.cause: Only the troops the player's ships carry fight in a naval mission; the party's other troops kept the player's side alive, so the map event went on.
regressions.fix: For the defeat the party is cut to a crew that all goes aboard (defeatTroops, recorded setup), against a pirate party three times its size.

regressions.failure: After the escape the party sat in War Sails' raft wait menu with campaign time stopped; the raft never reached the shore.
regressions.cause: The raft's wait menu starts campaign time itself (GameMenu.StartWait), which the probe's time-control lock refused.
regressions.fix: While the raft waits, campaign time runs as the wait menu runs it.
